concepts.def: Has a nucleus, cytoplasm, cell membrane, mitochondria and ribosomes.
Has all animal-cell parts plus a cell wall, chloroplasts and a permanent vacuole.
A bacterial cell with no nucleus; its DNA floats free in the cytoplasm.
The site of aerobic respiration, releasing energy for the cell.
Magnification = image size ÷ real size; used to study cells.
Cells differentiated for a particular job, e.g. red blood cells, nerve cells.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Cells — a core area of GCSE Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Cells brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Cells.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
